challenged_assumption: That the team's blended offence/defence rate is an adequate stand-in for an away starter who was not posted at capture, so that our_probability can be compared directly with market_probability.
case_against: The recommended probability of 0.5488894693325361 sits well above the market's 0.45276, yet the model had no away starter at all (away_sp_known false, away_sp_thin true) and fell back to a blended team rate. A large gap on a game where one side's pitching input is a fallback is more likely to reflect that missing input than a real edge. The market, with nine books, may already price a starter the model never saw, and the packet cannot tell us whether a probable was posted between the model run and the build time. The home starter averages 4.881 innings per start, so much of the game falls to a home bullpen whose recorded rate (5.3228) is higher than the away bullpen's (4.1159); the packet does not show how the model weighted that, and the roster transactions listed cannot be tied to either bullpen input. The pick's top score on the slate is a ranking of the model's own outputs, not independent evidence. I cannot say the pick is wrong, only that its key premise is unconfirmed.
